variants.headline: Building job cancelled part-way
variants.sub: The client has abandoned {project}, which {builder} was building.
variants.body:
The building job for {project}, undertaken by {builder}, has been cancelled part-way because {why}. The client has given up the plan. Readers judging {target} should distinguish this cancellation from a completed handover and consider what responsible stewardship means when an undertaking ends with the work unfinished.

A part-completed cancellation is a contract event, not a completed asset. Managers should distinguish the client's decision to abandon the plan from an assumed settlement of every obligation. Commercial scrutiny requires actual terms for financial consequences, rather than an automatic conclusion that the end of the job clears the account.

We defend {target} against an automatic adverse verdict. Giving up a plan need not prove every claim of poor judgment, and a fair assessment must consider more than the disappointment attached to an unfinished undertaking. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
